summary.headline: Blue Star Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 21% while operating profit grew about 10.5%; management targets at least 6.5% margin for FY27 with margins still under pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY and operating profit about 10.5%, driven by room ACs on an extended summer and early festive stocking. Margins stayed under pressure from material cost escalation that could only be partly passed on, with Unitary Products (UCP) margin falling to 2.3% in commercial refrigeration and segment-level margins down in both main segments. Management said Q2 was a consolidation quarter, with a 5% price increase from October and a product-portfolio rejig aimed at restoring the 6.5% company margin, though it gave no FY28 margin guidance. Net cash was Rs 289 cr versus net borrowings of Rs 417 cr a year earlier, and the order book rose to Rs 7,229 cr.

segments.name: Segment 1: Electromechanical Projects & Commercial AC Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,936 cr (+16.3% YoY); segment margin 6.9% vs 8.8%. Data center orders drove inflows, but billing was sluggish due to project delays; management guides 7%-7.5% segment margin.

segments.name: Segment 2: Unitary Products (Cooling & Purification, Commercial Refrigeration)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 898 cr (+29.4% YoY); segment margin 2.3% vs 6.2%. Only part of material cost increases passed on; commercial refrigeration still a degrowth and expected to be low single-digit to ~10% growth in H2.

segments.name: Professional Electronics & Industrial Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 97 cr (+51% YoY); margin 23.7% helped by provision write-back after MedTech sale for Rs 35.6 cr, completed Aug 31, 2026. MedTech FY26 revenue was Rs 41 cr.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company margin target of at least 6.5%; management called it tough and said Q4 (especially March pre-summer sales) will be decisive.
Room AC revenue growth for FY27 could be as high as 25%; management expects around 20-25% volume growth in H2, with 5% from price increases.
A 5% price increase effective October 2026 after about 18% cumulative input cost increase from January; a gap of about 5% remains even after October.

Data center order inflow estimated at Rs 10,000-12,500 cr for FY27 (about Rs 2,000 cr already secured); data center revenue to rise from about Rs 2,000 cr to Rs 4,000 cr in about 3 years; FY30 company revenue conservatively Rs 20,000 cr.
Full-year FY27 capex guided at up to about Rs 300 cr, including R&D and digital spend.
Segment 1 margin guideline 7%-7.5%; could reach 8.5% as data center execution scales, with indication expected in Q4.
Commercial refrigeration expected to grow about 10% in H2 and single digit for FY27; management sees revival from Q3.
No guidance given on FY28 margin; management said real indicator will be summer 2027.
capex_capacity: Full-year FY27 capex guided at up to about Rs 300 cr, including R&D products spend and digital expenditure.

Q2 cash-flow capex about Rs 130 cr in H1 per analyst estimate; depreciation rise attributed to amortised R&D, new warehouses and offices under lease accounting; management said current quarter depreciation is a normalised run rate.
Outsourcing of entry-level RAC products expected to rise from about 15% to up to 30% of volume.
Data center EPC work expected to add prefabrication and workshop capacity; projects run 8-9 months with good payment terms.
demand_pricing: Room AC industry Q2 standalone growth estimated at 35%-40% in primary sales; Blue Star primary growth about 42%.
Industry RAC H1 value growth about 30%; Blue Star about 28%-29%. Company says it regained market share from May onwards after losing share in April due to failed price increase.
Price increase of 5% announced for October; channel absorption not yet known, with dealers likely to have pre-bought in September.
Input cost inflation for RAC about 18% from January; commercial refrigeration requires 24%-25% price increase due to steel and plastic content.
Industry capacity is 1.7-2x demand; management expects competitive intensity and no pricing discipline.
Monsoon shortfall, farm income pressure and rising consumer finance rates are the main demand risks; US trade deal and West Asia resolution are potential tailwinds.
Infrastructure segment is about 20% of billing and is being deliberately shrunk; data center EPC market estimated at Rs 12,000 cr, chillers Rs 2,000 cr, liquid cooling CDU Rs 500 cr.

qa_highlights.question: Is 8%+ unitary products margin in H2 achievable to deliver the 6.5% company guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a tough but necessary task, dependent on price hikes, product rejig (value engineering, removing features, outsourcing entry-level SKUs) and scale; most revenue expected in Q4, especially March.

qa_highlights.question: Will schemes and competitor discounting hurt realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Schemes run almost year-round; average realisation is the key metric. Management expects no industry pricing discipline given capacity of 1.7-2x demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation rising sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikhil Sohoni said it includes amortisation of capitalised R&D across segments and lease accounting for new warehouses and offices; the current quarter run rate is normalised.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase is needed to match RM inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% input inflation from January; 13% average taken so far, so a gap of about 5% remains even after the October 5% increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the infrastructure drag and data center growth path?
qa_highlights.answer: Infrastructure about 20% of billing and shrinking; data center order target Rs 4,000 cr this year, Rs 8,000 cr by 2030; FY30 electromechanical revenue Rs 6,000-7,000 cr; Segment 1 margin 7-7.5% with possible upside to 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue US or Middle East data center opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not addressing US data center opportunities; chillers are dominated by US multinationals and liquid cooling technology is not held; US heat pump opportunity of up to USD 100 million remains intact.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY28 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given; management hopes for recovery but said the real indicator will be summer 2027; the industry should aspire to 10% margins.

risks_watch: Unitary products margin recovery from 2.3% to about 8% in H2 requires the October price increase to stick and the RM gap of about 5% to close.
Channel absorption of the October 5% price increase and possible demand tapering after festive pre-buying.
Execution delays and cost overruns in electromechanical projects; infrastructure billing shrinkage.
Commercial refrigeration revival dependent on FMCG and quick-commerce expansion; management calls it a never-ending story.
Depreciation and unallocable cost trend, and the outlook for capex of about Rs 300 cr.
summary.management_tone: Confident about direction but cautious on numbers: management said margins are the priority and called the 6.5% target tough, while refusing to give FY28 margin guidance. Tone was candid about past failures (lost April share, the Q1 margin shortfall), and evasive on commercial refrigeration and some data center questions.
key_quotes: We had indicated that we are confident of getting back to at least the 6.5%.
The demand is exceeding our expectations.
The electromechanical projects business, we are not chasing any market share. We will look at the margins and free cash flows, and that's all we will do, and it has to be profitable.
But I won't be able to give a guidance at all. The real indicator of that will be summer of 2027.

adds.what: No new company-owned plant or line capacity announced; data-centre EPC to add prefabrication and workshop capacity
Outsourcing of entry-level RAC products rising from about 15% to up to 30% of volume (sourcing shift, not owned capacity)

growth.why: Management guides RAC revenue growth of at least 25% for FY27 and data-centre order booking of about Rs 4,000 cr (Rs 2,000 cr already in hand), backed by a Rs 7,229 cr order book and a 5% October price rise, but no new owned capacity is quantified and margins remain under pressure (UCP margin 2.3%).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets at least 6.5% company margin and 7-7.5% Segment 1 margin, but UCP margin is 2.3% vs 6.2% a year earlier and needs about 8% in H2, with an ~18% input cost rise, only 13% passed on so far and a further 5% price rise from October leaving a ~5% gap.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new owned plant or line capacity was announced; only data-centre prefabrication/workshop additions and a shift of entry-level RAC outsourcing from about 15% to up to 30% of volume, and industry capacity is already 1.7-2x demand.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects 20-25% room AC volume growth in H2 and at least 25% RAC revenue growth for FY27, with Q2 primary growth about 42% and the Rs 7,229 cr order book up from Rs 7,120 cr a year earlier.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is capped at about Rs 300 cr including R&D and digital spend, and the call gave no new plant or line announcement; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 6.5% company margin and 7-7.5% Segment 1 margin, called the 6.5% target tough, and cited competitive intensity with no pricing discipline across an industry at 1.7-2x demand.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: UCP margin of 2.3% must reach about 8% in H2 for the 6.5% target, dependent on the October 5% price rise sticking after dealer pre-buying and a ~5% RM gap remaining, with Q4 (March) called decisive.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or model launch was discussed; product-portfolio rejig (value engineering, feature removal, entry-level SKU outsourcing) was mentioned without launch dates.

rows.label: 5% price increase from October 2026
rows.why: Effective October after about 18% cumulative input inflation from January, with 13% recovered so far and a ~5% gap remaining; channel absorption unknown after September pre-buying.

rows.label: Data-centre order inflow Rs 4,000 cr in FY27
rows.why: About Rs 2,000 cr already secured with management targeting another Rs 2,000 cr, against an estimated Rs 12,000 cr EPC market; the order book stood at Rs 7,229 cr at Sep 30, 2026.

rows.label: Commercial refrigeration revival
rows.why: Management expects about 10% growth in H2 and single-digit for FY27 from a degrowth base, but it depends on FMCG and quick-commerce expansion and a 24-25% price rise is needed for steel and plastic costs.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the Rs 7,229 cr order book and data-centre inflows, but cautious on margins, calling the 6.5% target tough and declining FY28 margin guidance; analysts pressed on UCP margin recovery from 2.3% to 8%, price-hike absorption and the depreciation rise.
